title: Festive Season Marketing for Breweries | Craft Beer School
desc: How breweries plan the festive season in India: seasonal beers, events, gifting, stock planning and responsible serving, within the ad rules.
teaser: The festive months are the busiest of the year for most taprooms. The planning starts long before the first diya is lit.
standfirst: From Navratri through Diwali to Christmas and New Year, the festive season brings more visitors, more gatherings and more gifting. Here is how we would plan a brewery's festive marketing so it sells beer without breaking the rules or the cold chain.
sections:
Festive marketing is a production question before it is a creative one. An ale needs roughly two to three weeks from brew day to a taproom tap. A lager needs closer to four to six, because of its cold fermentation and lagering. So a festive special has to be on the brew schedule well before the posters are designed.

Work backwards from the dates you care about. List the festivals that matter in your city, which differ a lot across India, then mark the brew day for each special and the last day you can change your mind. Dry days around elections and some festivals also vary by state, so check your local calendar and plan stock around them.
Pick one festive beer and give it a reason

One well made seasonal beats four rushed ones. Good festive beers in India tend to lean on familiar flavours used with restraint: a lightly spiced amber, a jaggery or coconut sugar ale, a chai spiced porter, an orange and cardamom wheat beer for the Christmas weeks. The spice should be a note, not a sweet shop. If guests need a second glass of water to recover from the cinnamon, the recipe needs work.

Give the beer a story that is true. Where the jaggery came from, why you chose that spice, what it pairs with on your festive menu. Our guide to beer brand storytelling has more on finding a story that is not invented.

The season is about gathering, so the taproom is your best channel. Ideas that work for many breweries:

  • A festive food pairing night with dishes from the region your guests come from.
  • A family friendly afternoon with a strong non alcoholic menu, so the whole group can come.
  • A release party for the seasonal beer with the brewer at the tap.
  • Corporate group bookings, which peak in this period, with fixed menus planned in advance.

Plan staffing and stock for the busiest evenings, not the average. A sold out seasonal on a Saturday night is a good problem. Running out of glassware or a cold keg is a bad one.

Gifting is huge in this season. Beer is awkward to gift in much of India because of how retail and licensing work. Where your licence allows takeaway, growlers and gift packs can sell well. Where it does not, merchandise and taproom vouchers do the job: glassware, a good T shirt, a tasting experience voucher. Gift vouchers also bring a new person through the door in January, when the taproom is quiet.

Check what your licence permits before you design any of this. Rules on takeaway and gift packs vary by state and change.

Direct alcohol advertising is restricted in India, so festive campaigns lean on the taproom, food, events and community rather than discounts on beer. Keep captions about the experience. Avoid anything that ties drinking to driving, religious imagery or anyone who could look under age. Our guide to alcohol advertising rules in India explains the position and why you should check the current rules before a paid campaign.

Plan the content calendar early: teaser for the seasonal beer, brew day photos, the release, the events, then thank you posts. Two or three posts a week through the season is plenty for most breweries.
Responsible serving is part of the brand

The festive season means more groups, more celebrations and more people driving home late. Say clearly, on menus and in posts, that you will call a cab for anyone. Train staff to stop serving someone who has had enough. Support them when they do it. Keep water on every table and make the non alcoholic list good enough that guests who do not drink feel welcome rather than tolerated. A good hop water, a house soda or a proper non alcoholic beer earns goodwill that lasts beyond the season.

Write down the numbers while the season is fresh: footfall on event nights, litres of the seasonal sold, voucher redemptions, which posts brought people in and what ran out. Next year's plan starts from that page. Most breweries repeat the same festive mistakes because nobody wrote them down.

The creative side of a festive campaign, the label for a seasonal beer and how it fits the core range, is where many breweries feel least confident. It is also the part that is easiest to learn.
faqs: When should a brewery start planning festive beers?
At least two months ahead. An ale needs about two to three weeks in the tank and a lager four to six. Design, printing and stock planning take time on top of that.
What makes a good festive beer for India?
A familiar flavour used with restraint, such as jaggery, cardamom, orange peel or chai spice in a balanced base beer. The spice should support the beer, not dominate it.
Can breweries run festive discounts on beer?
Alcohol advertising and promotion are restricted in India and rules vary by state. Most breweries focus on events, food and experiences instead. Check the current rules before any promotion.
How can a taproom welcome guests who do not drink?
Offer a real non alcoholic menu, such as hop water, house sodas or non alcoholic beer. Promote it as clearly as the beer list.
